---
title: "Transcriptomique spatiale : analyse de données et intégration scRNA-seq en Python"
subtitle: "CNRS Formation Entreprise · 24–25 November 2026 · ENS de Lyon / Spatial-Cell-ID"
---

**Data:** Visium spatial transcriptomics of human skin wounds ([GSE241124](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE241124)): 4 donors, each sampled as healthy skin and as a wound at day 1, day 7 and day 30, i.e. 16 tissue sections. On Day 2, a single-cell RNA-seq reference from the same study ([GSE241132](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE241132)) is used for sc–st integration.

**Paper:** Liu et al., *Spatiotemporal single-cell roadmap of human skin wound healing*, Cell Stem Cell 32, 479–498 (2025).

This page has three parts:

1. [Before the course](#before): get access to the computing resources. **Please do steps 1.1 to 1.4 before the course starts.**
2. [The two days](#days): how the course is organised.
3. [The reference notebook](#practical): the complete analysis, with all its outputs, and the data to run it.

## 1. Before the course {#before}

All the work is done on a virtual machine (VM) of the IFB cloud, **Biosphere**, with JupyterLab in your web browser. You do not need to install anything on your own computer.

### 1.1 Join the Spatial-Cell-ID group on Biosphere (a few days before the course)

Your request has to be validated by hand, so do this step **in advance**.

1. Go to <https://biosphere.france-bioinformatique.fr/>.
2. Click **Sign in** at the top right.
3. Click **Sign in** again.
4. Click **Accept conditions**.
5. Select your own institution.
6. Log in with your **institutional** username and password (no private e-mail account such as Gmail, Hotmail, Yahoo...).
7. Fill in the information: last name, first name, city and postal code. Leave the other fields as they are and accept.
8. You are redirected to a new page. Click the small person icon at the top right, then select **Groups**.
9. Click **Join a group** in the tabs at the top left.
10. Search for the group **Spatial-Cell-ID** and click the **+** button to apply.

That's it. Now wait for your application to be validated (the group will then appear in **Groups**).

### 1.2 Start a virtual machine

You can do this as soon as your membership is validated.

1. Connect to the [Biosphere catalogue](https://biosphere.france-bioinformatique.fr/catalogue/) (**RAINBio** tab).
2. Search for the [Jupyter appliance](https://biosphere.france-bioinformatique.fr/catalogue/appliance/131/).
3. On the appliance page, press the green button **RUN** (top right), then **Advanced Configuration and Start**.
4. Name your VM, and select **Spatial-Cell-ID** in *Group to use*.
5. In *Cloud*, select **meso-psmn-cirrus**.
6. In *Cloud Flavor*, select **standard.8c32g** (8 CPU cores, 32 GB RAM).
7. Press **Start Now**.
8. Switch to the **MyVM** tab. The VM is ready after about 15 minutes: you then see **https** and **Params** on the left. Press **Params** and copy your `JUPYTER_TOKEN`. Then press **https** and continue to the login screen, where you paste the token.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Keep the same VM for both days
Do not delete your VM at the end of Day 1. Your files are safe anyway (see 1.3), but with a new VM you would have to install the Python environment again (step 1.4).
:::

### 1.3 Where your files live: the permanent storage

Everything you need for the course is in a **permanent storage**, shared by all the VMs of the Spatial-Cell-ID group:

```
/home/jovyan/ifbdata/spatial_cell_id/CNRS_Formation_Entreprise/
├── environment.yml     the Python environment (step 1.4)
├── DATA_CNRS/          the data
└── trainees/
    ├── mrossi/         one personal folder per participant
    └── ...
```

- **The data** are already prepared for you in `DATA_CNRS`: the 16 Visium sections with clean names, the authors' spot annotation, and the scRNA-seq reference for Day 2. Read them from there; do not modify, move or write anything in this folder.
- **Your personal folder** is in `trainees`. Its name is the first letter of your first name followed by your last name, all attached (Mario Rossi → `mrossi`). **Save all your notebooks and results there.**

In JupyterLab, you reach it from the file browser on the left: `ifbdata` → `spatial_cell_id` → `CNRS_Formation_Entreprise` → `trainees` → your folder.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Never save your work outside the permanent storage
Your home folder (`/home/jovyan`, except `ifbdata`) and the local disk of the VM belong to the VM: when the VM is deleted, everything in them is lost. The permanent storage is independent of the VMs: if you delete your VM and start a new one, you find your folder exactly as you left it.
:::

### 1.4 Install the Python environment

In JupyterLab, open a terminal (*File → New → Terminal*) and run:

```bash
conda env create -f /home/jovyan/ifbdata/spatial_cell_id/CNRS_Formation_Entreprise/environment.yml
conda activate cnrs-st
python -m ipykernel install --user --name cnrs-st --display-name "Python cnrs-st"
```

- The first command takes **10 to 20 minutes** (it downloads PyTorch, needed by one of the Day 2 tools) and prints a lot of text: this is normal. Wait until you get the prompt back without an error.
- Quick test, still in the terminal: `python -c "import scanpy, squidpy, spatialdata; print(scanpy.__version__)"` should print `1.11.5`.

When you open a notebook, select the right kernel: click at the top right, where **Python 3 (ipykernel)** is written, and choose **Python cnrs-st**. If it is not in the list, reload the browser page.

::: {.callout-note}
## The environment belongs to the VM
Unlike your files, the environment is installed on the VM itself. If you start a new VM, you only need to repeat this step.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Why these exact versions?
Some recent releases are incompatible with each other (for instance, Harmony and the neighbour graph in scanpy). The versions in `environment.yml` were tested together: please do not update them during the course.
:::

## 3. The reference notebook {#practical}

The course is over: the step-by-step guide of the hands-on sessions is replaced by **the complete reference notebook**, the one we ran for the course, with all its outputs (figures, tables, interpretation of the results).

- [**Open the reference notebook (web version)**](notebooks/CNRS_ST_reference.ipynb), or download it to run it again: [`CNRS_ST_reference.ipynb`](https://github.com/sarnatas/skinwound/raw/main/cnrs-st/notebooks/CNRS_ST_reference.ipynb) (26 MB, right-click, *save link as*).
- It is one possible analysis, not *the* solution: if your choices (filters, parameters, option A or B) were different, your results are different too.

### Data to run it

- **Visium (16 sections):** GEO [GSE241124](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE241124). The folders are renamed `DonorX_Condition` by [`scripts/build_data_cnrs.sh`](https://github.com/sarnatas/skinwound/blob/main/cnrs-st/scripts/build_data_cnrs.sh).
- **scRNA-seq reference (Part D4):** [**download `sc_reference_mod.h5ad`**](https://github.com/sarnatas/skinwound/raw/main/cnrs-st/data/sc_reference_mod.h5ad) (66 MB) and put it in your `DATA` folder. It is a subset of GEO [GSE241132](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE241132) (donors PWH27 and PWH28, raw counts, the authors' annotation in `cell_type`): content and how it was built in [`data/README.md`](https://github.com/sarnatas/skinwound/blob/main/cnrs-st/data/README.md).
- **Environment:** [`environment.yml`](https://github.com/sarnatas/skinwound/blob/main/cnrs-st/environment.yml) (conda environment `cnrs-st`, see 1.4).

::: {.callout-note}

All the data come from Liu Z. et al., *Spatiotemporal single-cell roadmap of human skin wound healing*, Cell Stem Cell 32, 479–498 (2025), <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.stem.2024.11.013> (open access, CC BY 4.0). They are redistributed here for teaching only.
